item.title: Bridging the Beat presents "Go-Go Live AVL" — Sun Aug 9, 8:00 PM — Barley’s Downtown
item.description:
Experience the energy, culture, and history of Go-Go—the official music of Washington, D.C.—during an unforgettable weekend in Asheville! Don’t miss your last chance to experience the sound “that kept the whole neighborhood rockin” and the official music of Washington, DC. Take it back to the 90s with Next Gen Krank and DJ Supa Dan from 8:00 p.m. to midnight on August 9, at Barley’s Taproom. Admission is pay what you can ($20 suggested) and benefits our scholarship programs for local youth. Go-go comes alive across Asheville August 7-9, 2026, during Bridging The Beat, a three-day cultural exchange connecting Washington, DC’s go-go culture with Asheville’s Black cultural anchors, legacy neighborhoods, youth, public spaces, and community leadership.nd!
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: COMING Saturday August 29 | Keller & The Keels w/sg Tanasi — Mon Aug 10 — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Saturday, August 29 • 7 PM – 11 PM | From $45.70 Event Details and Tickets Musical Mad Scientist Keller Williams brings his Appalachian Psychedelic Bluegrass project, Keller & the Keels, to the stage on Saturday, August 29 with special guest Tanasi. Joining him are award-winning flatpicker Larry Keel and his rock-solid, in-the-pocket bass-playing wife, Jenny Keel. The trio—formed in 2004—has recorded three albums together (Grass, Thief, and Speed), and with only a handful of shows each year, every performance turns into a joyful, high-energy acoustic picking party. As Keller puts it, “We vowed from the beginning that we wouldn’t do it often so that when we did, it would be special—and it is.” 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of Grass, Keller & the Keels’ first album together. After two decades, Grass finally gets its first-ever vinyl pressing—available on site and ready to roll

item.title: AT South at Devil's Fork Gap to the Historic Shelton Graves site: Fitness Hike. — Wed Aug 12, 9:00 AM
item.description: The Asheville Hiking Group This is a pretty out & back 11.5 mile forest hike on the Appalachian Trail with about 2,600' of elevation gain, with some views throught the trees. We will take a short spur trail to the Civil War era Shelton Grave site and stop for a snack before returning. **Pace:** We will hike at a brisk pace averaging approximately 3mph adjusting for steepness of grade and rugged trail conditions. Please be comfortable with this distance, elevation and pace. **Dogs;** Friendly dogs ok. **Car Pool or Follow to the Trailhead:** Meet at the Park and Ride parking lot, Exit 17 I-26 at 8:30am. Please post if you plan to carpool, or to meet at the trailhead at 9:00 am. . **Directions**: Drive I-26 W from Asheville to the Flagpond, TN exit.. Take a left at the end of the ramp then go right when you reach a T intersection at Flag Pond. Continue until you see a left turn onto HWY 352W. If you miss the turn you will see the entrance to Rocky Fork State Park a short distance after.
